## Part B-Basic Data Types
```{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L        # the L suffix forces an integer
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i

typeof(x)
typeof(y)
typeof(z)
typeof(w)
typeof(v)
```
```{r}
class(x)
class(y)
class(z)
class(w)
class(v)
```
```{r}
mode(x)
mode(y)
mode(z)
mode(w)
mode(v)
```
##Question #3: x <- 42 and y <- 42L look almost identical, but typeof(x) and typeof(y) give different answers. Explain the difference in your own words.
```{r}
x <-42
y <-42L

typeof(x)
typeof(y)
```
##Because x is double and y is integer because x and y is simillar but y has a L at the end.

## Part C-Type Conversion (20 min)
```{r}
num_string <- "123"

as.numeric(num_string)
typeof(num_string)
class(num_string)
mode(num_string)
```
```{r}
as.logical(0)
as.logical(1)
```
```{r}
bad_string <- "hello123"

as.numeric(bad_string)
typeof(bad_string)
class(bad_string)
mode(bad_string)

```

## Part D - Strings, paste(), and pastet0()

```{r}
first_name <-"Juan"
last_name <-"Dela Cruz"

print(first_name)
print(last_name)
cat(first_name, last_name)
```
```{r}
full_name <-paste(first_name,last_name)
full_name
paste0(first_name,last_name)
```
```{r}
paste(first_name,last_name, sep = "-")
```
```{r}
age <- 21
paste0(full_name, " is ", age , " years old")
```
##Question#7: based on my observation paste0 cconnects both Juan and Dela Cruz.While paste will just put a space between two arguaments.
##Question#8: No, it did not cause an erro because paste0 automatically converts any argument into a character string before joining them.
```{r}
##"5" + 5 
```
```{r}

```
